test_title: PYST 14: RRB Group D Official Paper GS - (Held On: 04 Dec, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: A coin is placed on a card covering a glass. When the card is flicked quickly with a finger, the coin falls straight into the glass. What does this situation show?

options.text: The coin moves because the card pushes it
The flick applies a force directly to the coin
The coin remains at rest due to inertia when the card moves away
The coin and card both move away due to inertia

solution:
The correct answer is __**The coin remains at rest due to inertia when the card moves away.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Inertia:** The phenomenon of the coin falling straight into the glass when the card is flicked demonstrates the principle of **inertia**. Inertia is the tendency of an object to resist changes in its state of motion or rest unless acted upon by an external force.
 
• **The Coin’s Rest State:** Initially, the coin is at rest along with the card. When the card is flicked quickly, the card experiences a force that sets it into motion. However, the coin remains in its rest state due to its **inertia**.
 
• **Lack of Horizontal Force on the Coin:** The flick primarily applies force to the card, not directly to the coin. Therefore, the coin does not gain significant horizontal motion and falls straight down into the glass.
 
• **Gravitational Force:** Onc
